subject: Post-call recap — dedicated pool sizing, isolation requirements & next steps
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Timmons <alex.timmons@medpulse.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap — dedicated pool sizing, isolation requirements & next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and the proposed path forward so your team can share internally.

Key pain points you shared
- Variable tail latency on your current hosted endpoints for live triage workloads (esp. during morning spikes).
- Strict PHI handling needs: VPC isolation, customer-owned KMS, and audit logging for retention 7 years.
- Predictable unit cost for high-throughput imaging/triage pipelines (batch and streaming mix).

Goals you want to achieve
- Stable p95 latency under 120 ms for inference paths serving structured triage (50–70 qps sustained).
- P99 budget target near ~300 ms; prioritize availability > latency if trade-offs required.
- Provisioned, isolated capacity (no multi-tenant neighbors) with contractual uptime and incident SLAs.

Rough sizing & configuration (initial proposal)
- Reserved pool: baseline of 8 x A100-class GPUs (equivalent capacity) dedicated to MedPulse.
- Burst policy: allow 2x temporary burst (subject to capacity) to cover peak traffic.
- Canary plan: start with a 48-hour production canary running a subset of traffic (5–10 qps) then ramp over two weeks.

SLA targets (provisional)
- 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool (monthly).
- P95 latency SLO: 120 ms; P99 latency target: 300 ms (monitor-only for first 30 days).

Mutual action plan (owners & next steps)
- Alex / MedPulse: share procurement contact + estimated timeline for a 6–12 month reserved commit; confirm PHI compliance checklist items (due: 2026-12-02).
- Redwood (Rohan): drop a draft SOW and pricing range + canary run plan (attached).
- Redwood (Lauren): provide a canary run playbook and network/VPC wiring checklist.
- Both: schedule a technical deep-dive next week to align on KMS and connectivity.

Attachments: MedPulse_Sizing_Workbook_v1.xlsx (workload samples + tokenization assumptions), draft SOW docx.

If that aligns, I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive and share the SOW draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rohan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Timmons <alex.timmons@medpulse.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medpulse.com
Date: 2026-11-28T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — dedicated pool sizing, isolation requirements & next steps

Rohan — thanks for the clear recap. That matches what we captured internally. A few clarifications and asks from our side:

1) PHI scope: all inference inputs/outputs are PHI. We will need VPC-only connectivity (no public egress), customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS), and proof of audit log retention. Can you confirm Redwood’s support for those?

2) Sizing: the 8 x A100 equivalent makes sense as a starting point. Our internal benchmark (on a smaller model) suggests we may need an extra 20% headroom for peak peak (30–45 minute windows). Can you include burst handling options and how billing for burst capacity will be handled?

3) Procurement: looping in procurement (procurement@medpulse.com) — they’ll own the timeline and PO. Our target is to have a reserved pool in place and pilot running by 2027-01-10.

4) Security questionnaire: please send the SOC2 + infra questionnaire — I’ll aim to return it within 10 business days.

We’re also happy to start with a 6-month pilot (reserved capacity + SLA-lite) before committing to an annual reserved contract.

I can do a tech deep-dive Tue 12/1 between 10–1 PT or Wed 12/2 after 2pm PT. Which works for your team?

—Alex
Alex Timmons
Head of ML Infrastructure | MedPulse
alex.timmons@medpulse.com
+1 (617) 555-3344

Alex — will pick up the technical pieces. Short notes from the architecture perspective: 

- VPC & KMS: we support VPC peering/private connectivity and integration with customer-managed KMS (AES-256 + HSM-backed keys). We’ll include the wiring checklist in the deep-dive.
- Data flow: suggest applying prefix caching for recurrent prompt patterns in triage to cut token cost ~35% — we’ll show measured numbers in the canary.
- Canary plan: 48-hour smoke (10% traffic), 7-day ramp to 50% of targeted qps, then full ramp over two weeks. We’ll instrument p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1000-requests metrics.
- Burst model: recommend a soft burst pool with pre-authorized credit (billing shows as OTC for burst minutes) — Ben will share the draft burst pricing table.

Action items I’ll own: canary runbook, VPC/KMS wiring doc, and the instrumentation dashboard template. I’ll post those to the Drive folder before the deep-dive.

Thanks — speak soon.

Lauren Bishop
